skill.name: bash-defensive-patterns
skill.description: Guides users in writing defensive Bash scripts with strict mode, input validation, safe file handling, cleanup traps, logging, idempotency, and dependency checks.
skill.summary: Provides practical patterns for writing safer, more reliable Bash automation.
skill.author: wshobson

content.value_statement: Bash scripts often fail on edge cases, unsafe variables, and partial cleanup. This skill provides practical defensive patterns for robust automation and CI/CD scripts.
actual_capabilities: Explains Bash strict mode and error trap patterns.
Shows safe variable quoting, arrays, and conditionals.
Provides patterns for argument parsing, logging, and dry-run support.
Demonstrates safer temporary file handling and atomic writes.
Covers dependency checks, idempotency, and process cleanup.
limitations: Does not execute, lint, or test scripts automatically.
Examples require adaptation before production use.
Focuses on Bash, not POSIX sh or other shells.
Does not replace security review for privileged automation.

use_cases.title: Harden CI Scripts
use_cases.description: DevOps engineers can add strict mode, logging, and cleanup to deployment pipelines.

use_cases.title: Review Automation Utilities
use_cases.description: Platform teams can compare existing Bash scripts against defensive patterns before release.

use_cases.title: Teach Safe Shell Practices
use_cases.description: Technical leads can use the examples to coach teams on reliable shell scripting.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Safe Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the bash-defensive-patterns skill to outline a minimal Bash script template for copying files safely.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Script
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the bash-defensive-patterns skill to review my Bash script for quoting, strict mode, cleanup, and argument parsing issues.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Deployment Helper
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the bash-defensive-patterns skill to design a deployment helper with dry-run mode, structured logging, dependency checks, and rollback points.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Team Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the bash-defensive-patterns skill to create a readiness checklist for Bash automation that handles signals, temp files, and idempotency.

output_examples.input: User asks for a safer script template.
output_examples.output: The response recommends strict mode, required variable checks, structured logging, and a cleanup trap before adding business logic.

output_examples.input: User asks why a CI script failed silently.
output_examples.output: The response identifies missing pipe failure handling, weak logging, and absent error traps, then proposes safer patterns.

output_examples.input: User asks for deployment script review.
output_examples.output: The response flags unquoted paths, unsafe cleanup, missing dry-run support, and dependency checks to add before release.

best_practices: Use the skill before writing high-impact automation, not only after failures.
Adapt examples to local paths, permissions, and operating system behavior.
Pair generated scripts with ShellCheck, tests, and a human review.
anti_patterns: Do not copy destructive examples into privileged scripts without safeguards.
Do not treat the examples as complete applications.
Do not ignore portability when scripts must run outside Bash.

faq.question: Does this skill run shell commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides written guidance and examples. It does not execute commands by itself.

faq.question: Can it replace ShellCheck?
faq.answer: No. Use it with ShellCheck and tests for stronger coverage.

faq.question: Which shell does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Bash scripts. Some ideas may need changes for POSIX sh.

faq.question: Is it useful for CI/CD?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers strict mode, cleanup, logging, dry runs, and dependency checks for automation.

faq.question: Can beginners use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples introduce common defensive patterns with practical explanations.

faq.question: What should I verify before production use?
faq.answer: Verify permissions, paths, destructive commands, dependencies, and behavior on the target operating systems.
